text:
The gain error points to the op-amp tail. Both a1 and a2 are about 15% low (simulated/ideal ≈ 0.846 for each), so the common cause is reduced open-loop gain, not the input resistors. M5 is the tail current source, and it is in triode: Vds = 0.226 V against Vdsat = 0.546 V. The input pair's Vgs (0.674 V) leaves only about 0.23 V across M5, which cannot support its overdrive. Triode operation lowers the tail current to 26.7 µA (the mirror ratio from M6 predicts about 41 µA) and reduces the input-pair gm, which lowers loop gain. M5's W/L (2.02/2.34) gives too much Vdsat for this headroom. The sensitivity lists do not include M5, but they only show first-order effects of the other devices, and the operating-point data singles out M5.

{"ranking": ["M5", "M6", "M8"], "fault": "Tail current source M5 is sized with too much overdrive (W=2.02, L=2.34 gives Vdsat about 0.55 V). Its drain sits at about 0.23 V, so it is pushed into triode. Its current drops from the mirror-expected ~41 uA to 26.7 uA, which reduces op-amp gm and open-loop gain and causes the ~15% closed-loop gain shortfall on both inputs. Fix: increase M5 W (about 4x, to lower Vdsat into saturation) or shorten its L, then recheck the bias and gain."}
